summary: An announcement that UCSB offered a Data Reconfiguration Service, an experiment in reformatting data streams passing between two network programs. Users define a form describing changes such as inserting or deleting fields, packing characters, or translating character sets. The RFC explains how to use the service.

plainLanguage.summary: UCSB announced a service that changes data as it passes between two network programs. Users describe the changes in a form, and the service applies them to the stream.

questions: what was the data reconfiguration service
how does drs reformat network data
subtitle: How UCSB's Data Reconfiguration Service changed data between network processes.

tldr.problem: Network processes can use different data formats. UCSB announced a service experiment to transform data between them.
tldr.mechanism: A user defines a form of transformation rules. DRS connects two processes, applies those rules to the stream, and forwards the result.
tldr.outcome: The RFC describes the service and its command interface; the unit metadata lists its status as Unknown.

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 437's status as Unknown. The RFC describes an experimental data-reformatting service at UCSB.

sections.title: The Data Reconfiguration Service
sections.content: RFC 437 announces the Data Reconfiguration Service (DRS), an experiment at UCSB for transforming data streams between network processes. The RFC says it can connect processes with different input and output interfaces, so they can exchange data as if directly connected.
sections.plainLanguage: DRS passes data between two programs and changes it on the way. The programs can use different input and output formats.

sections.title: Forms and Transformations
sections.content:
A form describes the changes to apply to one direction of a message path. The RFC lists examples such as inserting or deleting fields, rearranging fields, handling variable-length strings, packing characters, and translating character sets.

A compiler turns each form into machine-independent instructions, and an interpreter runs those instructions. The DRS Time Sharing System provides the user interface.
sections.plainLanguage: A form lists the changes to make to a stream, such as removing a field or translating characters. A compiler prepares the form, and an interpreter applies it.

sections.title: Running and Managing a Form
sections.content:
Users connect to DRS/TSS, define and store forms, compile them, and run them against network connections. The RFC describes simplex runs with one one-way path and duplex runs with a form for each direction; it also documents commands, connection methods, and job controls.

The service and its server Telnet are reachable through socket 1281 decimal. The RFC describes the service as available at the time of publication.
sections.plainLanguage: Users define a form, compile it, then tell DRS which network connection to use. A one-way run uses one form; a two-way run uses one for each direction.
